Do NOT tune thresholds or weights from this sample.' checkIns.summary: A live member asked directly (via chat, not the audit lane) why Legacy's contracts were so much more expensive on some nights, pointing at that night's real published book: MU $1020 CALL @ $24.88 ($2,488/contract) next to BMNR/ETHA/MARA at $52-$111/contract. Traced the root cause: pickChainContract (deterministic-edition.ts) picks the strike NEAREST TO SPOT (ATM) with no cost-awareness beyond the hard $35/share MAX_OPTION_PREMIUM_PER_SHARE ceiling -- that ceiling exists (PR-N15) only so a strong candidate is never dropped outright, never as an affordability target. Since ATM premium scales roughly linearly with the underlying's own price, the identical 'closest to spot' rule produces wildly different dollar costs across tickers purely as a function of stock price. Pulled MU's real live chain (spot $1017.75, Sep-25 expiry) to ground the fix: 0.50Delta ATM = $2,488/contract, 0.16Delta = $557/contract (still a real directional trade), sub-0.06Delta = $100-150/contract range (genuine lottery territory, not comparable to the other tickers' native cost). Shipped and merged PR #5344 same session: pickChainContract gained a strictly opt-in preferAffordable parameter -- when true, prefers the nearest-to-spot strike that ALSO clears premium <= $8/share AND |delta| >= 0.15, falling straight through to the exact unchanged ladder when nothing clears both (including when the row has no delta data at all, e.g. some UW-sourced rows). All 4 Legacy call sites (main synthesis loop, diversity-hedge swap, forced-contrarian re-score, buildRescuePlays) opted in; pickChainContract's other real caller, Vector (vector-play-candidates.ts/vector-dte-horizon.ts), is untouched by construction since it never passes the new parameter -- confirmed via Vector's own test suite passing unmodified.
checkIns.assessment: This is a genuine, member-facing product-quality fix, not a correctness bug -- every previously-published contract was legitimate and under the hard cap, just needlessly expensive on high-priced underlyings for no reason related to setup quality. The delta floor (0.15) is the load-bearing design choice: Swing's own HORIZONS config (horizons.ts) already documents having tried and reversed a pure cheap-OTM stance for exactly this reason (a 0.35Delta/[0.25,0.50] 'cheap OTM banger' policy was replaced with 0.50-0.75Delta because a multi-session thesis needs an instrument that tracks the underlying, not a low-delta lotto) -- reused that lesson rather than re-learning it. 7 new tests (regression proving default behavior unchanged, the preferred pick firing correctly, the delta floor correctly excluding a cheaper-but-too-low-delta strike, a no-delta-anywhere chain being a total no-op, an already-affordable ATM strike being unaffected, a no-gap-between-bars fallback case, and one full end-to-end buildDeterministicEditionPlays test). Full src/features/nighthawk/** suite: 1876/1876 pass. tsc clean, next lint clean. CI (verify + CodeQL) went green in ~7 minutes; merged via direct GitHub MCP merge_pull_request since automerge.yml's own merge step is known-broken per this file's own CLAUDE.md notes.
checkIns.action: PR #5344 merged (sha 7bc6884, squash). Staged finding logged: docs/audit/findings-staging/2026-09-21-legacy-contract-cost-preference.md. NEXT-SESSION MARKET-OPEN VALIDATION NEEDED: once a future edition actually contains an expensive underlying (>~$500/share) as a candidate, verify live that the published contract lands in the cheaper preferred band (or falls back honestly to ATM if nothing clears the delta floor) rather than assuming the fix works from the unit tests alone -- this session had no real expensive-underlying candidate in tonight's actual book (MU/BMNR/ETHA/MARA are all already-committed picks from before the fix shipped, so tonight's book itself won't show the fix's effect; the next NEW edition build is the first real chance to observe it live). PREFERRED_OPTION_PREMIUM_PER_SHARE ($8) and MIN_PREFERRED_CONTRACT_DELTA (0.15) are reasoned, evidence-grounded defaults from one live chain pull, not backtested/calibrated -- a future cycle should not treat them as settled without real forward-graded evidence.

checkIns.summary: First real D_pull_status read of the trading day (13:22Z cycle, morning-confirm cron has now run for 2026-09-21's edition) — this transitioned from the correctly-SKIPPED state every cycle since 04:21Z to a real, non-trivial result: 3 of tonight's 4 plays (MU, ETHA, MARA) were pulled pre-open (INVALIDATED<->pulled=true, coherence check passes on all 4), only BMNR confirmed. Pulled real pulled_reason text off GET /api/market/nighthawk/edition rather than treating the bare INVALIDATED verdict as self-explanatory: all 3 pulls cite the SAME underlying mechanism -- a Cortex fresh-veto on [gex-walls], specifically 'long target path crosses dominant call wall ... inside 0.5x expected move' -- with real, specific numbers for each (MU: wall 1050, 18.58% of ladder gamma, 14.73pts above spot 1035.27, inside a 14.77pt expected move; ETHA: wall 21, 29.44% of ladder gamma, 0.39pts above spot 20.61, inside a 0.77pt expected move; MARA: wall 14, 23.05% of ladder gamma, 0.12pts above spot 13.88, inside a 0.85pt expected move). ETHA and MARA additionally cite a real pre-market gap re-anchor (both gapped above their published entry range overnight) layered on top of the same gex-walls veto.
checkIns.assessment: Outcome-honesty read: this looks like the protective mechanism doing its actual job, not a bug -- in all 3 cases the play's own long target sits behind a real, sizeable dominant call wall (18-29% of that ticker's own ladder gamma) within a tight fraction of the expected move, which is exactly the shape of setup Cortex's gex-walls veto exists to catch (a target that would need to punch through real dealer gamma resistance to be reached). The reasoning is specific and falsifiable (real wall strikes, real gamma %, real distance-vs-expected-move math), not a generic catch-all excuse. That said, a 75% same-morning pull rate citing the identical gate is a real data point worth tracking, not dismissing -- per this file's own 3-instance noise threshold, ONE morning like this is not yet a pattern; if the SAME gex-walls-veto-heavy pull rate recurs on a 2nd and 3rd distinct trading day, that crosses into 'is this gate now systematically too aggressive, or is the current book genuinely running into more gamma-wall resistance than usual' territory worth digging into. Also worth flagging for context, not as a defect: MU was the exact ticker flagged in this session's earlier member complaint about contract cost (fixed same-day via PR #5344/#5355) -- that fix targets CONTRACT SELECTION (which strike gets picked), completely orthogonal to this morning's SETUP-level gex-walls pull (whether the play should trade AT ALL pre-open); the two are unrelated mechanisms and MU being invalidated here is not evidence the contract-cost fix did or didn't work as intended.
checkIns.action: No fix needed -- this is a first, coherent data point, not a confirmed pattern or a bug. Logging the real pulled_reason text (not just the bare verdict) so a future cycle checking whether gex-walls pulls are becoming a recurring pattern has the actual evidence to compare against, per this file's own 3-instance discipline. Watch for the SAME gex-walls-veto shape recurring on the next 2 distinct trading days before treating it as a calibration question.

As of this cycle, 3 of 4 published plays -- MU, ETHA, MARA -- are ALL INVALIDATED via the identical mechanism (each one's long target path crosses its own dominant call wall, each inside its own 0.5x expected-move band): MU crosses 1050 (18.58% of ladder gamma) 14.73pts above spot 1035.27 (0.5x EM=14.77pts); ETHA crosses 21 (29.44%) 0.39pts above spot 20.61 (0.5x EM=0.77pts); MARA crosses 14 (23.05%) 0.12pts above spot 13.88 (0.5x EM=0.85pts). Only BMNR survives CONFIRMED (re-anchored to a pre-market gap, no gex-walls veto cited). B_marks still GREEN on all 4 (BMNR/MU/ETHA/MARA marks all live, two-sided, in-range) and D_pull_status coherence (Redis-cached vs DB-merged read) still agrees on all 4 -- this is a real, correctly-computed product outcome, not a data/wiring bug.

But the MAGNITUDE is new: this is the first time in the live journal that a MAJORITY (75%) of one night's published book has been invalidated by the same single Cortex gex-walls fresh-veto mechanism on the same trading day. Per the 3-instance discipline this is still one trading day's data (today, 2026-09-21) -- the individual MU instance was already noted this morning, so this is a same-day escalation in scope rather than a new distinct day -- so NOT escalating to a findings-staging fix yet. checkIns.summary: Repeat-GREEN cycle on the healthcheck matrix (same MU/ETHA/MARA INVALIDATED + BMNR CONFIRMED state as 16:23Z/16:36Z/16:52Z) -- no new state transition. But traced the ROOT CAUSE of the gex-walls-veto escalation flagged at 16:23Z (knownOpenItems.gexWallsVetoRate_2026_09_21) while idle, and it is a real, high-confidence correctness finding, not just a magnitude WATCH item. src/lib/nighthawk/cortex/fetch.ts: vectorHorizonForCortexCommit(horizon: CortexCommitHorizon = '0dte') maps 'swing' -> Vector horizon 'monthly', everything else (including the default) -> '0dte'. The Legacy morning-confirm cron (src/app/api/cron/nighthawk-morning-confirm/route.ts:410) calls fetchCortexInputs(ps.ticker, direction, { now, timeoutMs: 4_000 }) with NO horizon option -- so it defaults to '0dte'. Repo-wide grep of every fetchCortexInputs(...) call site (morning-confirm, zerodte/exit-sync.ts, zerodte/cortex-gate.ts, bie/cortex-read.ts x2) found ZERO callers anywhere that pass horizon:'swing' -- the 'swing'->'monthly' branch is dead code, never exercised. Consequence: the shared gex-walls fresh-veto (src/lib/nighthawk/cortex/sources/gex-walls.ts, wallPathCheck, WALL_PATH_BLOCK_EM_FRAC=0.5) gates Legacy's multi-day-hold plays (DTE ~5-30 per the Legacy->Swing promotion window) against a SAME-DAY (0DTE) options-implied expected move, not one scaled to the play's actual holding horizon. A 0DTE expected move is dramatically narrower than a multi-day one (~sqrt(days) scaling -- a 10-day hold's real EM is roughly 3x a 0DTE EM), so 'target path crosses a dominant wall inside 0.5x expected move' fires far more readily than a correctly-scaled band would allow -- very likely the direct mechanical cause of today's 3-of-4 (75%) invalidation rate (MU/ETHA/MARA all cited this exact veto). For 0DTE's own commits (exit-sync.ts, cortex-gate.ts) the '0dte' default is CORRECT (0DTE literally trades same-day) -- this is not a bug there. It is specifically a Legacy-caller bug: the morning-confirm cron never opts into a horizon matching what it is actually gating.
checkIns.assessment: HIGH-CONFIDENCE, HIGH-PRIORITY finding -- but explicitly NOT fixing it myself this cycle. Two reasons: (1) it is a live-picks-gating-logic change (changes which Legacy plays get pre-open INVALIDATED), squarely inside this session's standing 'no scoring/ranking/gating changes without fresh explicit authorization' constraint and the Legacy mandate's own 'Ambiguous/live-picks-logic -> report, hold' escalation rule -- not a small/unambiguous CARVE-OUT fix. (2) the correct target horizon is itself a judgment call, not mechanical: 'swing'->'monthly' already exists and would be a large improvement over '0dte', but Legacy's real DTE floor (~5 days per the promotion-path gate) sits closer to VectorDteHorizon's 'weekly' option than 'monthly' for the shortest-dated plays -- picking between adding a genuine 'legacy' CortexCommitHorizon case (mapped to 'weekly' or 'monthly'), reusing the existing but never-yet-proven 'swing' case as-is, or scaling the EM lookup to the PLAY'S OWN per-ticket DTE rather than a fixed bucket, is a real design decision. Also worth flagging: the same default-0dte gap likely reaches Swing too (its own commit path was not traced this cycle -- out of this lane's scope -- but if Swing also never passes horizon:'swing', the identical mechanical bug would apply there).
checkIns.action: ESCALATING, not fixing. Logged as knownOpenItems.legacyGexWallsHorizonMismatch_2026_09_21 (high priority, supersedes/explains the earlier same-day gexWallsVetoRate_2026_09_21 WATCH entry -- that entry's n=1-trading-day caution still holds for confirming the OUTCOME impact, but the MECHANISM is now understood, not just observed). No code touched this cycle. Recommend as the next authorized fix (pending operator/explicit go-ahead per standing constraints): either add a Legacy-specific CortexCommitHorizon case or thread the play's real per-ticket DTE into vectorHorizonForCortexCommit's Vector-horizon choice, with an A/B proof (same fixture inputs, old-vs-new horizon) that no OTHER cortex source/behavior changes -- same rigor precedent as Workstream C D4-extra's geometry/premium_cap capture fix. Continuing the routine 15-min cadence.

ZETA/ACN are presumably live only because some other desk/user coincidentally holds the exact same OCC as a real open position; FORM/UTHR aren't, so they're 100% dependent on Polygon's snapshot-endpoint lag with no WS backstop. VERDICT: the 30s LEGACY_QUOTE_STALE_MS staleness flag is working exactly as designed here -- correctly refusing to show a fake-fresh mark for genuinely provider-lagging data, not a bug to silence.
